input.brief: concept preview for a fresh juice shop in Gokul Nagar, Bhiwandi: fruit juices, cold drinks and ice cream, open every day 6:30am to midnight

direction.name: One motif
direction.idea: Take one shape from the subject and let it run the whole system. A drilling tool's octagonal cross-section becomes the buttons, the image masks and the loader. A two-account money app becomes two circles that recur as icon, inline dot and section colour. A café's striped awning becomes every band on the page. Look at the product, the logo, the object or the word in the headline and find the simplest geometry in it (a circle, an arc, a chamfer, a stripe, a notch, a ring). Then use only that shape, at three or four very different scales, everywhere a designer would normally reach for a generic rounded rectangle.
direction.composition: Hero: the motif appears once at enormous scale as a flat filled shape, cropped by the viewport (a circle 120vh across entering from the right, a chamfered block filling the lower half), with a short headline at 6–8vw and one supporting sentence set on the remaining ground, left-aligned on a shared margin. Through the page the motif returns as: the mask for every photograph (via `clip-path` or `border-radius` made from the same geometry), the shape of the primary button, the bullet beside list items at text size, and one full-width band that separates the two halves of the page. Sections use simple two-column or single-column layouts so the shape is the only thing with character.
direction.typography: A clean geometric or grotesk face that echoes the shape (round bowls for circles, squared terminals for chamfers). Medium weight; headings 6–8vw in the hero and 3–4vw after.
direction.colour: The motif carries the accent colour at large scale, flat. Everything else is ground and ink. A second motif colour is allowed only if the subject has a real pair (two accounts, two modes).
direction.imagery: Photographs appear inside the motif's shape. If there is product interface to show, it sits on a flat colour stage shaped by the motif. Draw the shape with CSS or a simple inline SVG path; do not draw illustrations.
direction.richness: One shape at many sizes. The giant cropped shape gives the hero mass and colour without a single image.
direction.pitfalls: One motif means one. A circle here, a hexagon there and a blob behind is the generated look this replaces. The motif must come from the subject and you must be able to say from where in one clause.

hero.name: Giant cropped shape
hero.blueprint: A plain ground with one shape at enormous scale: a photograph of the subject (its material, its object, its place) cut with `clip-path` to the simplest geometry found in the subject (a circle, a ring segment, a chamfered block, an arch), never a drawn or filled shape. It is about 110vh tall on columns 7–12, its right side on the right page margin and its centre at 55% of the height, so the hero's top and bottom crop it. The headline sits on the bare ground on columns 1–6, vertically centred, on the left margin: two lines at clamp(64px, 6.4vw, 100px), heavy weight, tracking -0.03em. Beneath it comes one supporting sentence at 19px, then the single action as the dealt button. The dealt navigation runs across the top.
hero.mobile: The shape moves to the bottom: the full content width between the page margins, its top at 56svh, cut only by the hero's bottom edge. The headline sits above it at 11.5vw on two lines on the page margin, starting 15% down, with the sentence at 16px and the button beneath. The navigation folds behind a Menu word.
hero.headline: Two lines of two or three words each, up to about 12 characters per line at 6.4vw.

palette.name: Graphite and orange
palette.note: Graphite and cool light-grey sections alternate, graphite taking about two thirds, and photographs are chosen calm and low in colour so nothing competes (in full colour where the pictures carry the colour; greyscale only where section 0 deals black-and-white). Safety orange marks the buttons, one thick solid bar across the top of the page and the highlighted item in a list or chart.

type.name: Josefin Slab, a slab

text.settings: weight 400 for running text, 600 for emphasis and buttons, leading 1.5, 60-72 characters a line

type.note: A slab. A 1.25 scale from a 16px body; the hero's display step is about 7.6vw at 1440. Six steps and no others: small, body, lead, sub, head, display. Josefin Slab does every job, told apart by size and weight (500 for display, 400 and 600 in text). Load only the weights listed; a weight the face lacks is faked by the browser and the inspector fails it.

photos.title: Interior and table
photos.note: rooms, windows, chairs, cups, food and tabletops

photos.alt: Shadow of a window frame and potted plants falling on a sheer cream curtain in soft daylight
Cream ceramic table lamp on a glossy side table, low sun throwing long shadows across a white wall
Cappuccinos with latte art, water glasses and a slice of cake on a round dark wood cafe table
Small cup of latte art on a white saucer seen from above on weathered grey wooden planks
Two pairs of hands holding a black coffee and a milky coffee on a white marble table with sprigs of flowers, seen from above

motion.name: Pushed line
motion.description: One line of very large type, the name or the claim, is pushed sideways by the scroll rather than by a clock: it travels from 12% right to 12% left of its place while it crosses the screen, linear and locked to the scrollbar, and reads whole at the middle of its run. One per page, never across running text, and the words must never be cropped at the moment the line sits in the middle of the screen. Build with animation-timeline: view() on the line and a translateX keyframe; static where scroll timelines are unsupported and under reduced motion.

sections.name: Right-half paragraph, lone photo
sections.blueprint: No heading. On a 12-column grid with 5vw margins, one statement paragraph of 45–70 words occupies columns 7–12 only, set at clamp(24px, 2.2vw, 34px) with leading 1.25 and a first-line indent of 3em. Its top edge sits 18vh below the section top. Columns 1–6 stay empty except for a single square photograph, 20vw wide, in columns 1–3, placed so its top aligns with the paragraph's last line and it hangs below the text by most of its height. A five-line note at 14px, 180px wide, sits in columns 1–2, 96px beneath the photograph. Section padding is 160px top and bottom. Nothing is centred: the paragraph's left edge is the midpoint of the page, and later text blocks on the page may reuse that line. Holds one paragraph, one photograph and one note.
sections.mobile: The paragraph comes first at 22px, full width with 20px margins and no indent. The photograph follows at 62% width, pushed to the right margin, in a 4:5 crop instead of square. The small note sits to its left, bottom-aligned with the photograph, in the remaining 30% of the width.

sections.name: Day tabs, banded agenda
sections.blueprint: A two-line heading at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), first line in the soft ink and second in full ink, with the booking button on the same row at the far right. 56px below, left: a 150px column of stacked day tabs, each a filled block 150 by 64px with 6px gaps showing the weekday at 16px and the date at 13px; the active tab takes the darkest fill with inverted text. Right, from 190px to the right margin: the day's sessions as alternating tone bands, each 76px tall with an 8px radius and 4px gaps, the two tones one step apart. Inside a band, on fixed column starts: the time at 20px with tabular figures, 20px from the left; the title at 18px in medium weight at 22%, with a one-line note at 13px in the soft ink under it; speaker names right-aligned at 14px beside up to three overlapping 32px round portraits.
sections.mobile: The heading stacks above a full-width button. Day tabs become a horizontal row of equal filled blocks, sticky under the top edge. Each band stacks time over title over speakers with 16px padding and grows to fit; portraits sit at the band's top-right corner.

sections.name: Photo pair with split captions below
sections.blueprint: Two near-square photographs in columns 1 to 6 and 7 to 12 of the content width, a 24px gutter, each about 644x640 in the dealt corner with a 6% inner parallax. Under each photograph, 16px down, a two-column caption: a title at the lead step over two lines starting at the photograph's left edge and a body-step line or two starting at its midline. The photographs arrive with the dealt entrance. Hover: the photograph zooms 1.03 inside its crop. Phone: the photographs stack at 4:5 and each caption becomes a title over its paragraph. House rules for it: Captions sit under the photographs, never on them. Photographs are art-directed, never documentary.

sections.name: Address in display rows
sections.blueprint: The contact block is a stack of five full-width rows, every one set at the same size, clamp(44px, 6vw, 88px), regular weight, left-aligned with a 20px inset and leading 1.0: the building or venue name, the street, the city with postcode, the opening hours as one compact line, the phone number. Each row is about 150px tall with the text sitting in its lower third; rows are told apart by alternating two flat tones of the section colour as full-width bands, or by 28px of space alone. A sixth row holds a one-word greeting at the same size followed, 24px to its right and centred on the x-height, by a solid round button 0.9em across with an arrow, which opens the email or booking link. Street and phone rows are links (map, call). No heading and no form. Optionally, one small round photograph sits at the right end of the first row.
sections.mobile: Rows at 9.6vw with 16px insets, about 84px tall; the hours break onto two rows (days, then times). The greeting row becomes a full-width band in the accent colour with the round arrow button at its right end, 56px across.

references.name: SSTR - Friction Reduction
references.idea: Drilling hardware treated like precision consumer tech: a chamfered octagon taken from the tool's cross-section drives the buttons, icons and loader.
references.hero: The captured first viewport is the preloader: a 2 by 2 grid with hairline dividers, top-left quadrant solid orange with the slash-prefixed name at 5.6vw in black bold grotesk; top-right dark with a plus-sign dot grid and an orange square beside a percentage; bottom quadrants hold wireframe octagon stacks under small labels. The real hero is a full-bleed grey 3D render of a steel downhole tool rising from bottom centre. A two-line uppercase headline at about 3.5vw in light grotesk sits left-anchored at mid-height, with a short paragraph and an orange chamfered-corner button below. A slim bar holds logo left, five small caps links, globe and contact right.
references.type: ABC Monument Grotesk: bold for the loader mark, but headlines are regular or light uppercase with tight tracking at roughly 36 to 50px over 14px body. Uppercase labels at 10 to 11px carry a square orange bullet. Statistic numerals jump to about 6.7vw in a thin weight.
references.colour: #18191b #eff0f1 #ff5a2a #2f3032 #c3c4c8 — Graphite and cool light-grey sections alternate; one safety orange marks buttons, bullets, the loader block and the highlighted chart series. Renders are desaturated steel so orange never competes.
references.imagery: Desaturated 3D renders of drilling tools, full-bleed in the hero and as a long drill string bending along a well path; thin wireframe octagon line drawings as service icons; a chart drawn in dots.
references.layout: Content sits inside vertical hairline rails about 35px in from each edge, with sections subdivided into two or three bordered cells. Dark and light sections alternate. Text blocks are left-aligned and narrow; a pinned well-path sequence breaks the grid with a full-bleed scene.

sections.description: Light grey section inside vertical hairline rails. An uppercase two-line heading at about 2.4vw sits top-left with an orange chamfered button under it. Below, three equal columns divided by hairlines, each about 230px tall: a wireframe line drawing of stacked octagons in the upper half, then an uppercase title at 13px and three lines of small grey body. No fills, no icon circles, no shadows.

Graphite section split into two bordered cells. Left cell, vertically centred: a tiny bracketed before-and-after range in caps, a statistic at about 6.7vw in thin grotesk, a one-word label and an orange chamfered button. Right cell: a line chart drawn entirely in dots, white for the baseline and orange for the improved run, with faint axis labels and a two-item legend using short colour bars.

Pinned full-viewport dark scene. A 3D drill string enters at top-left, runs down, bends through ninety degrees and continues along the bottom to the right edge, with bright tool segments spaced along it. A text block right of centre holds a small orange-bulleted label, a four-line uppercase statement at about 2vw and two lines of body. Bottom edge: a back-to-start link left, a chevron scroll cue centre, a skip link right.

steal: Derive one shape from the product (here a chamfered octagon) and reuse it for button corners, icons and loader graphics.
Draw charts with dots rather than lines and reserve the accent colour for the one data series you want read.
Turn the preloader into a branded four-cell grid that previews the site's colour blocks and wireframe icons.
references.media: A full-bleed 13s monochrome loop of a drilling tool descending over grey sand covers the whole fold with the text straight on it at the left, oversized for parallax. Below: a full-bleed WebGL chapter with the caption right of centre and a depth gauge at the edge, line-drawn icons in three equal cells, dot-plot charts beside big figures zigzagging per row, a 4:1 product strip under a giant product-code heading, and 3:2 case photographs in a right-hand column; 33 images and 3 videos, 0px radius.
references.motion: On desktop the video plays from 400ms while every text line shows as a solid orange bar the size of the line, like redaction, and the type replaces the bars by 1.2s. Under Lenis the hero video parallaxes at scrub 2, heads rise as masked lines over 0.6-0.82s expo.out at a 0.04-0.06 stagger, chart dots switch on one by one (1004 rects at 0.15s), stats roll digit columns, the WebGL chapter is step-locked with skip controls, and buttons fill with a clip-path sweep over 0.375s; there are 10 reduced-motion rules.

references.name: Midnight
references.idea: The headline's circles are literally pictured: one blurred dark ring, sliced into horizontal bands, becomes the hero, the demo panel, the session cards and the footer.
references.hero: No navigation at all. A canvas fills the full width and the top 90% of the viewport: a huge out-of-focus dark navy ring on drifting taupe, sage and terracotta, cut into horizontal bands about 78px tall that are slightly offset like blinds. On the vertical centre line, starting 58px from the left, sit a small rounded-square line icon and a one-line headline at 48px in cream. On the same baseline, starting 59% across, a two-line 17px statement whose first sentence is white and bold while the rest drops to half opacity. The cream page background shows as a 90px strip at the bottom. No button.
references.type: Public Sans only, weight 500, tracking −0.04em. Headline 48px, mid-page statement about 38px on five centred lines, body 13–17px. Signature device: within one paragraph the first sentence is full strength and the remainder faded, replacing the usual heading-plus-subhead pair.
references.colour: #f4efe6 #07172a #867768 #687674 #a8735c #faf7f1 — Warm cream pages against midnight navy; the gradient mixes muted taupe, sage and terracotta around the dark ring. A peach-cream fills the small pill button. No bright accent anywhere.
references.imagery: An animated blurred ring gradient with band displacement and fine grain, used full-bleed in hero and footer, inset with 8px corners as the demo panel, and miniaturised onto three portrait session cards. No photos or UI screenshots.
references.layout: 30px side margins. Sections alternate between full-bleed gradient and cream type-only screens. Section headers split into left title and right small paragraph. Text blocks are short and often occupy one half of the width, leaving the other empty (the FAQ sits entirely in the right half).

sections.description: A full cream viewport with one centred paragraph of five lines at roughly 38px, about 820px wide. Only the opening sentence is dark; the remaining words are pale and darken progressively with scroll. Later, three small portrait cards, each about 115×180px with a mini gradient, a date at the top and a two-line label bottom-left, fan across the right side of the text, overlapping it with a soft shadow.

Header row: a two-line title at 34px on the left, a three-line 12px grey paragraph in the last fifth on the right. Below, a gradient panel spans the full content width, about 650px tall with 8px corners, holding a centred question at 34px in cream, a one-line caption, and an email capsule with an inline peach button; a small play capsule sits centred near its bottom edge.

A left-aligned two-line lead uses the dark-then-faded sentence device. Under it a two-by-two arrangement with no cards or borders, columns starting at 0 and 50%: each item is a 24px pale rounded-square icon, a quoted question as a 13px semibold title, then three or four lines of grey 12px text about 300px wide. A waitlist capsule floats fixed at bottom centre.

FAQ rows with hairlines and chevrons occupy only the right half of the screen above. The footer is the gradient again, full-bleed and about 190px tall: a two-line cream statement at left, an email capsule with inline button at right on the same line, and a row of tiny grey legal links along the bottom.

steal: Slice a soft blurred gradient into horizontal bands with small offsets so a familiar glow becomes a recognisable, ownable texture.
Replace heading-plus-subhead with one paragraph whose first sentence is full contrast and the rest half opacity.
Remove the nav from the hero entirely and put headline left and supporting line right on one shared baseline at mid-height.

references.name: Madie
references.idea: A burgundy-and-cream bakery brand in which the madeleines themselves, cut out like specimens, become the menu.
references.hero: A dark, warm photograph (iced coffee with a logo sticker and a glazed madeleine on a wooden counter, burgundy tiles behind) fills a rounded-corner frame inset 20px from every edge on a cream page; the subject sits right of centre. In the left column, starting 42% down: a small star-rating line, then a three-line uppercase headline at 5vw in a heavy geometric sans, the first two lines outline-only and the third solid cream, a three-line paragraph, and a row with a pink pill button and an underlined text link. Top-left: menu icon and script logo. Top-right: a three-language pill toggle. Bottom-right: a circular text badge.
references.type: Dazzle, a heavy geometric uppercase, for headlines at 72px, used both solid and as an outline stroke; Cottorway, a slightly wide geometric sans, for 14px body and for a light italic accent word. A brush-script logo. Tracked capitals near 10px for labels.
references.colour: #f6efe6 #3d0012 #5c0a23 #ff99d3 #160b0a #e8a530 — Cream and deep burgundy alternate by section across wavy boundaries. Bubblegum pink is reserved for buttons, the active filter pill and carousel arrows; the product cut-outs supply every other colour.
references.imagery: A moody warm-graded hero photo; individual madeleines shot from above and cut out with soft shadows as small menu thumbnails; white line drawings (dog in beret, cafe table); rounded photo cards stacked at a tilt; a map redrawn in burgundy.
references.layout: Centred intro, a left-anchored story block on burgundy, then a two-column menu inside a container about 60% of the width. Section edges are curved waves rather than straight lines. Rounded frames and a sticky header with filter pills recur throughout.

sections.description: Cream field, everything centred. A tiny tracked-capitals label flanked by two short rules, then a two-line heading: the first line outlined uppercase in burgundy at about 4.5vw, the second a lowercase light italic of the body sans, solid. Three short paragraphs at 13px follow in a column about 45% wide. The section ends in a burgundy wave rising from the bottom, with a white line-drawn dog perched on the curve.

Burgundy field patterned with a faint tone-on-tone repeat of the logo. Left: a white line illustration, a three-line paragraph with bold phrases, two round pink arrow buttons and a slide counter. Right: a stack of portrait photo cards with rounded corners, the top one tilted a few degrees and the others fanned behind it. The bottom edge curves back to cream.

A sticky row of three pill filters beside the logo, the active one filled pink. Each category has an outlined uppercase label at left, an item count at far right and a hairline beneath. Items run in two columns: a 60px cut-out madeleine at left, then a bold uppercase name and a two-to-three-line italic description; some carry a tiny best-seller note or a pink allergen tag. No prices and no boxes.

Deep burgundy. The left two-thirds is an interactive map restyled entirely in burgundy and pink with rounded corners, the script logo as its pin and a small address card overlaid bottom-left. The right third is a rounded outlined panel listing opening hours, phone and email under tiny capital labels, plus two social icons. The script logo, large and white, is centred below, followed by a tracked-capitals legal line.

steal: Set a headline with its first lines as outline strokes and the last line solid, so emphasis falls on the final phrase without a size change.
Replace the stock map with one restyled in the brand's two colours and use the logo as the pin.
Build the menu from small cut-out product photos beside bold names and italic notes in two columns, with no cards.

scenes.name: Letter bar floods the ground
scenes.summary: One short statement holds on a single line in the page's display face with one straight letter (I, l, i, 1 or a T's stem) on the dead centre of the screen; from the first frame the camera zooms on that letter: the whole line scales up round its stem, the letter in its own proportions and the words growing more slowly as they leave past the screen's edges. Once the letter is wider than a third of the screen and taller than it, only its bar is left, a column of ink that keeps widening; the next section's opening statement arrives inside it at about half-way while the outgoing words' edges are still in frame, the column reaches full bleed by 80% and the statement grows to its resting size as the camera lands, so the next ground arrives through the inside of a letter with no seam and no hold of plain colour. A hand-over for pages with no pictures, in any sector.
scenes.place: Between two sections, as the hand-over from the page's ground to its ink (the intro to the offer, the about to the prices, the work to the contact). The section before ends on the page's ground; the section after continues on the ink straight under the statement the flood ends on, with little top padding. Once per page, with a quiet section before it.
scenes.content: No pictures. A statement of 2-4 words, 12-22 characters, on one line, set at display size (96px or more on a desktop, nearly the full width on a phone), with a straight-stemmed letter near its middle: I, l, i, 1 or a T, never O, S, A or any letter with a bowl or a counter. Long words that push the pivot far from the middle shrink the line (its longer half round the stem sets the size). The next section's opening statement, 4-8 words in two lines at most at every width, and an optional sentence of 12-24 words under it, both in the ground's colour on the ink. One ground and one ink, 7:1 or better both ways; no accent, no second colour on any word.
scenes.options: hold 1.1 (1-1.5); phoneHold 1 (0.8-1.2); pivot, the letter's index in the statement (spaces counted) or the letter itself (a span.lbf-pivot in the markup wins; else the straight letter nearest the middle); third 0.3 (0.2-0.4) share of the hold by which the stem is a third of the width; half 0.5 (0.4-0.6) share by which it is half the width (the next statement arrives about here); flood 0.8 (0.6-0.8) share by which the column fills the screen; grow 0.5 (0.3-0.8) the words' scale as a power of the letter's; nav '', the selector of a fixed header, and navClass 'is-flooded', which it gets while the ink covers it; scrub 0.5, true with Lenis and on touch; phone 'same' | 'rest'. Tokens: --lbf-size, --lbf-gutter, --lbf-next-size, --lbf-next-measure, --lbf-pad.
scenes.phone: The same zoom with phone numbers: the line spans nearly the whole width round its stem (a 12px gutter); the letter stays a letter, ends in view, until it is taller than the screen (about 0.55, near 30 times its size, repainted sharp rather than stretched from a small layer); the stem is a third of the width by 0.3 with the outgoing words' edges in frame; full bleed by 0.8; hold 1. Screens under 480px tall get the finished composition.

nav.text: A fixed bar that starts tall and collapses on scroll. At rest it is 96px high with no fill over the hero: a typographic wordmark at the left (about 212px wide, the display face at the head step in the heaviest dealt weight, type only, never drawn), four one-word links at body size (16px), weight 600, 32px apart, and at the right margin the one action as the dealt button in the accent, 44px tall (on a shop the basket as a word before it). Over the first 120px of scroll the bar eases to 64px and takes a solid band of the page ground; the wordmark scales and cross-fades (200ms) into a 40px monogram chip, and the four links fold into Menu as the dealt button in the ink beside the action, so content never runs under bare letters. Where the hero's headline is the name, the first screen shows the monogram chip alone. On a phone: a 72px bar with the wordmark about 150px wide, a Menu text button and the action, collapsing to 56px with the monogram the same way. House rules for it: No announcement line above the bar; the wordmark is type only (no drawn mascot or illustration); the bar is 96px, about a tenth of the first screen; Menu and the action are the dealt button, not outlined icon buttons or a second shape; the collapsed bar is opaque.
nav.signature: On the first screen the 96px bar carries a head-size type wordmark and four links; over 120px of scroll it collapses to a 64px solid band where the wordmark has become a 40px monogram chip and the links have folded into Menu.
nav.name: Tall wordmark bar that collapses

footer.text: A closing line over columns: the closing line at the h2 step (the action as a statement, four to seven words, two lines at most) with the one button under it; 96px below, three or four short columns at body size: the sections, the contact (the email, a phone only if the brief gives one), the place or the social links, the legal links with Image credits; the © line at the foot. On the surface tone, as tall as its content, about 60svh at 1440, so the line, the button and the columns share one screen. On a phone the columns stack in pairs.
footer.signature: A closing line at the h2 step with its one button, then three or four short columns 96px below, on the surface tone, about 60svh, all on one screen.

cards.text: Cards laid on the table like a dealt hand: three to five filled cards with the dealt corner in one row, centred, 40px apart, each turned about its centre by an angle fixed for its place (-2.5°, 1.5°, -1°, 2°, -1.5°), never overlapping, their corners 16px apart or more and inside the margins. In turn the ink (lettered in the ground colour) and the surface tone, the first in the ink. Each holds, 28px in, the name at the h2 step in the display face's heaviest weight, one line at body size and the price or the fact at the h4 step at its foot, as tall as its words; where the items have pictures, the picture inset 16px at the top at 4:3. The deal plays once as the row arrives (the cards fly from one squared pile to their places, 90ms apart), and a still shows them dealt. Hover or focus straightens a card and raises it 8px. For the three things to try, the dishes of the day, the hosts, a small range. On a phone one card to a row at the content width less 16px, at a third of the angle.
cards.signature: Three to five cards lying at small fixed angles in one row, in turn the ink and the surface tone, each name at the h2 step in the heaviest weight.

buttons.text: Soft rectangles: 8px radius, 44-48px tall, 20px padding, the text face at 15-16px weight 600, filled with the accent; hover lightens the fill one step, press darkens it. The second action is the same shape in the surface tone with ink letters.
buttons.signature: 8px-radius buttons 44-48px tall in the accent; the second action the same shape in the surface tone.

corners.text: A 16px radius on cards and panels; pictures at 16px or square inside a card.

spacing.text: Standard: 16-20vh between sections (about 144-180px at 1440 by 900, 96-120px on a phone), page margins 32-48px at 1440 and 20px on a phone.

treatment.text: Pictures in natural colour, as shot, with matching light; no filters, no tints, no grain.

interaction.text: One working tool the visitor would really use, built from the subject's content (a price or size calculator, a booking with real dates, a filter over the real list). Not a toy, not a demo of the page's own design. It works on a phone with a thumb and has a plain fallback.

clip.text: One moving picture of the subject: a muted loop with a poster frame and a pause control, used once, large. Only if an honest clip of this subject exists.

entrance.name: Exposure
entrance.summary: the photograph's light and colour come up from pale
entrance.sees: The type is in place at once. The photograph starts pale, as if over-exposed (dim on a dark page), and its real light and colour come up in about a second.
entrance.markup: Use it on a mid-tone or dark photograph: on a pale one the change barely shows and reads as a glitch. A photo treatment's filter goes on the frame, never on the img or video.

byImagery.photo: A photograph or a clip. base.css animates the img's or video's own filter, so a caption in the frame stays at full ink.

below.label: Pictures take their colour
below.rule: Large pictures (data-reveal="picture", four at most) go from 20% saturation to full colour once as they enter, over 900 ms with ease. No travel, no scale, and text never moves.

moves.name: Char blur scrub
moves.description: A short headline of at most 10 words at the head step on two lines (or a statement of 14 words at most at 36px or less on three lines), ink on the ground, split into characters. It is scroll-linked (0.6 smoothing) over 400-720px of scroll as the block travels from 85 to 40 percent of the viewport: each character comes into focus from blur 4-12px to blur 0, staggered left to right and line by line so the focus runs like a wave of three to five letters. The text is in full ink and in place from the first frame (nothing fades or moves in; arrival is the dealt entrance's): only the focus changes. On the way out the same values reverse once the block passes 20 percent from the top. It is fully crisp before it has to be read. One type step, no colour change per character. Phone: blur peaks at 8px, splitting limited to 80 characters to protect the frame rate; the parent keeps an aria-label with the whole text. House rules for it: No accent word, no coloured letters; letters never move or fade in, only their focus changes, and the real words are present whole; the headline is two lines at most or the statement 36px or less on three lines.

moves.name: Late word slides in
moves.description: A hero headline of three to five words at the display step over two lines. The last word starts about 96px below its line, fully visible from the first frame, so the sentence already reads whole; across 60svh of scroll, in a hero held that long, it slides up (scrubbed, eased) into its line and closes the gap. Every word shares one face, colour and weight. The hero still fills the first screen alone. On a phone the word starts 64px below and runs over 50svh. House rules for it: The sliding word has exactly the same face, colour, weight and style as the rest (no accent word); it is a real word of the sentence; the hero still fills the first screen alone and reads whole in the first frame.
moves.phone: Display step on the phone; the word starts 64px below and runs over 50svh.

moves.name: Rounded tile goes edge
moves.description: A picture tile (16:9 or 21:9, 1370px wide at 1440) sits inset by the page margin on each side with the dealt corner as the section arrives. Over the next 650-720px of scroll (while it is sticky, or as its top travels from 90 to 30 percent of the viewport) it widens to the full 1440px: clip-path inset(0 var(--margin) round var(--radius)) to inset(0 0 round 0), the height holding or growing from 80svh to 100svh. The corner eases to 0 so it ends edge to edge. Text for the section sits below the tile and is simply there (the dealt entrance decides whether it arrives); no caption sits on the picture. Phone: inset by the page margin with the dealt corner, widening to the full 390 over 60 percent of the scroll distance. House rules for it: A picture tile in the dealt corner, no outline, no caption box on the photograph; the pin, if any, is under two screens.

typeNote.name: One book serif, flat scale
typeNote.description: Faces: one book serif (transitional or old-style) at 400 with a true italic kept for whole quotes. The top step is only 40-56px (2.75-3.9vw at 1440), leading 1.0-1.1, tracking -0.01em, two lines at most; then 44 / 32 / 24px, body 18px at leading 1.5, small 14px. Ratio 1.5-2.8x. Almost no size contrast, so rank comes from space, position and cards on the one surface tone; headings in sentence or title case. A small sans at 14px in sentence case for captions is optional. It reads like a printed book, so the dealt hero's large photograph has to fill the first screen. Colour: the dealt ground and ink, ink one step off full contrast; the accent on the primary action and links only. Motion: headlines arrive with the dealt entrance; hover darkens ink. House rules for it: Italics only for whole quotes, never for a word in a headline; no paper-and-terracotta pairing: ground and accent are the dealt ones.
